study type: case-control study with a nested cohort study
exposure: Women with vitamin D deficiency and history of pregnancy complicated by PD: (1) observed from pre-gravid stage, (2) observed from the 1st trimester of pregnancy.
Bsml (A>G, rs1544410) polymorphism of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) gene
outcome: Pregnancy complications (e.g., early gestosis, fetoplacental perfusion violation, signs of amnionitis, low placentation, placental hyper/hypotrophy, preeclampsia)
cohort: Two-stage study: (1) 56 pregnant women with PD and 40 with physiological pregnancy, (2) 57 women with vitamin D deficiency and history of pregnancy complicated by PD (27 observed from pre-gravid stage, 30 from 1st trimester).
finding: Women with placental dysfunction had lower vitamin D levels and a higher frequency of the A/G genotype of the VDR gene polymorphism compared to those with physiological pregnancies; timely cholecalciferol supplementation from the pre-gravid stage was associated with fewer pregnancy complications.
